ledger.x: c. 1215 BC: Edom appears in the record. Infobox 'Established: c. 13th century BC'; the page cites 'the list of the Egyptian pharaoh Seti I from c. 1215 BC' as the earliest mention and says the nation 'flourished between the 13th and the 8th centuries BC'. It names no founder.
734 BC: Edom pays tribute to Assyria.
c. 609 BCE (bridged): Assyria's overlordship ends. No page opened dates when Edom stopped paying Assyria; the year mirrors the neo-assyrian-empire dossier's close of the 734 tributaries.

c. 609 BCE (bridged): Edom is under Babylon. The Nebuchadnezzar page has the kings of Ammon, Edom, Moab, Sidon and Tyre meeting at Jerusalem in 594 BC to discuss throwing off Babylonian control; the start of Babylonian overlordship is undated. c. 553 BC: the Kingdom of Edom ends. Infobox end c. 553 BC; the Nabataeans later 'established their own kingdom in what used to be Edom by the first half of the 2nd century BC' and 'truncated province of Idumea' is attested by 365.

wars.name: Saul's war against Edom
wars.outcome: The page mentions 'their defeat by King Saul of Israel in the late 11th century BC'; no territorial result is dated.

wars.name: Amaziah of Judah's war against Edom
wars.outcome: Amaziah 'defeated Edom'; the Red Sea ports of Eilat and Ezion-Geber are said to be Judah's 'under Amaziah's time (796-769 BC)'.

wars.name: Revolt of Ammon, Edom and Moab against Nebuchadnezzar II
wars.outcome: 'In 587 BC, Ammon, Edom and Moab likewise rebelled'; the Edom page puts the 'destruction of the kingdom by Nebuchadnezzar II in 587/86 BC'.

wars.name: Nabonidus's Arabian campaign
wars.outcome: Edom captured in 553 BC; Nabonidus then fights the king of Dadanu and takes Tayma, where he lives in exile from 552 to 543/542 BC.

certainty.note: No Edomite boundary is described on any page opened; the plateau, the Arabah and the Negev settlements are named only as places.
